/-!
# Erdős Problem 498

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/498](https://www.erdosproblems.com/498)
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er45] Erdős, P., _On a lemma of Littlewood and Offord_. Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (1945), 898-902.
- [Kl65] Kleitman, Daniel J., _On a lemma of Littlewood and Offord on the distribution of certain
  sums_. Math. Z. (1965), 251-259.
- [Kl70] Kleitman, Daniel J., _On a lemma of Littlewood and Offord on the distributions of linear
  combinations of vectors_. Advances in Math. (1970), 155-157.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos498

/--
Let $z_1,\ldots,z_n\in\mathbb{C}$ with $1\leq \lvert z_i\rvert$ for $1\leq i\leq n$. Let $D$ be an
arbitrary disc of radius $1$. Is it true that the number of sums of the shape
$$\sum_{i=1}^n\epsilon_iz_i \textrm{ for }\epsilon_i\in \{-1,1\}$$
which lie in $D$ is at most $\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$?

A strong form of the Littlewood-Offord problem. Erdős [Er45] proved this is true if
$z_i\in\mathbb{R}$, and for general $z_i\in\mathbb{C}$ proved a weaker upper bound of
$$\ll \frac{2^n}{\sqrt{n}}.$$
This was solved in the affirmative by Kleitman [Kl65], who also later generalised this to
arbitrary Hilbert spaces [Kl70].

See also [395].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1268917deaaaa0d674f651287027baa26cea9920/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos498.lean#L2006"]
theorem erdos_498 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (z : Fin n → ℂ), (∀ i, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) → ∀ c : ℂ,
      {ε : Fin n → ℤ | (∀ i, ε i = -1 ∨ ε i = 1) ∧
        (∑ i, (ε i : ℂ) * z i) ∈ Metric.ball c 1}.ncard ≤ n.choose (n / 2) := by
  sorry

end Erdos498

reformulations.difference: Relative to Kleitman's strict-length formulation and the pinned formal proof, the file uses ‖zᵢ‖ ≥ 1 with an open unit disc. The linked proof uses ‖zᵢ‖ > 1 with a closed unit disc. This is an equivalent boundary convention; the file directly matches Erdős's original interior-of-the-disc formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: There are finitely many admissible sign patterns. For the open-disc formulation, choose 0 < r < 1 bounding the distances of all contributing sums from the center, then scale every vector and the center by 1/r. The vector norms become strictly greater than 1 and all contributing sums enter the closed unit disc. Conversely, for vectors of norm strictly greater than 1, choose 0 < r < 1 with r‖zᵢ‖ ≥ 1 for every i. Scaling by r sends all sums in the closed unit disc into the open unit disc. These inclusions preserve the upper-bound implication in both directions, including n = 0. Proved as Review498.open_iff_closed in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. An additional proof in /workspace/review/exact_bridge.lean derives the exact reviewed statement from the pinned external theorem.

review.notes: No mathematical defects found. The primary sources explicitly use interiors and count sign choices with multiplicity. Lean checks establish finiteness of the counted set, so Set.ncard's infinite-set default is unreachable; n = 0 is harmless. Direct small-instance proofs and enumeration through n = 8 confirm the counting conventions. The pinned external proof and the exact-statement bridge compile with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The community database records problem 498 as proved (Lean), consistent with the file. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/498 was blocked by Cloudflare, so the comparison used the original papers; the 1970 Hilbert-space result was checked through its published reprint abstract.
